mainTopic: The fast-day ברכות, rules for כהנים about wine during and after the time of the מקדש, and how often a מלך, a כהן גדול, and a כהן הדיוט cut their hair
overview: This amud opens with the closing words of a discussion from the previous amud: זכרונות and שופרות are said only on ראש השנה, on the יובל, and in wartime. The גמרא then explains the משנה's extra ברכות for a fast day. It shows that אליהו's 'עננו ה׳ עננו' counts as crying out, and that יונה comes before דוד so the series can end with 'מרחם על הארץ'. Next, a ברייתא explains why the אנשי משמר may drink wine only at night, while the בית אב on duty may never drink. From this it rules that a כהן today must avoid wine for a day, a week, or a whole year, depending on how much he knows about his family's turn. רבי says that logically wine should always be forbidden, and אביי says כהנים drink today following רבי. The גמרא then explains the ban on haircuts during the watch, and how often a מלך, a כהן גדול, and a כהן הדיוט cut their hair, learning thirty days from נזיר. It asks why כהנים need not cut their hair today and compares it to wine. It then begins to challenge that comparison from רבי and אביי, and the conclusion comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing words of the previous discussion on זכרונות and שופרות
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends: זכרונות and שופרות are said only on ראש השנה, on יום כיפור of the יובל, and in a time of war.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...only on ראש השנה, in the יובל years, and in a time of war.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of a discussion that began on the previous amud. It lists the only occasions when the ברכות of זכרונות and שופרות are said: ראש השנה, the יובל, and wartime. This is why רבי יהודה held they are not needed on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (only) shows that this line limits a practice. It does not start something new. It closes the earlier topic, so the next line can return to the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year, when the שופר is blown
Jubilee years; the שופר is blown on יום כיפור of the יובל

phrases.english: only on Rosh HaShana,
phrases.notes: Continues a sentence that began on the previous daf

phrases.english: and in the Jubilee years, and in a time of war.
phrases.notes: Sefaria explains: Yom Kippur of the Jubilee year

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a discussion carried over from the previous daf
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practice under discussion is limited to ראש השנה, the יובל, and wartime.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה on the first extra ברכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: for the first extra ברכה one says 'מי שענה את אברהם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the first ברכה he says: 'He Who answered אברהם' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to open a new discussion. This line sets up the next step, which brings a ברייתא about these ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a תענית ציבור, extra ברכות are added. Each one mentions someone whom הקב״ה answered in a time of trouble. Quoting the first one points us back to the whole list.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the quote continues as in the משנה

phrases.english: For the first one he says:
He Who answered Abraham, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the list of fast-day ברכות in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first extra ברכה mentions that הקב״ה answered אברהם.

steps.title: A ברייתא: some swap the endings of the שמואל and אליהו ברכות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says some people end the אליהו ברכה with 'צעקה' and the שמואל ברכה with 'תפילה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: some people switch. They give 'שומע צעקה' (Who hears crying) to אליהו, and 'שומע תפילה' (Who hears prayer) to שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another version of the endings. In the משנה, the שמואל ברכה ends with 'צעקה' and the אליהו ברכה ends with 'תפילה'. Some people reverse these two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה pairs each ברכה's ending with how that person called out to הקב״ה. The 'switchers' pair them the other way around. That raises a question: do the new pairings match the פסוקים? The next step asks exactly this.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. In the משנה: שמואל = צעקה and אליהו = תפילה. The ברייתא's 'switchers' make it אליהו = צעקה and שמואל = תפילה.

phrases.english: It was taught: some reverse
'crying' for Elijah,
and 'prayer' for Samuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another version of the wording of the ברכות quoted from the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some people end the אליהו ברכה with 'שומע צעקה' and the שמואל ברכה with 'שומע תפילה'.

steps.title: Challenge: where is 'crying' written about אליהו?
steps.stepSummary: Both words fit שמואל. But for אליהו only 'prayer' is written, not 'crying'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for שמואל: the פסוק uses 'prayer' about him and also 'crying' about him. But for אליהו, 'prayer' is written and 'crying' is not. So how can his ברכה end with 'crying'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'switchers'. Giving 'prayer' to שמואל is fine, because both words appear about him. But nothing in the פסוקים says אליהו 'cried out'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule assumed here is simple: a ברכה's ending should match how the person called out in the פסוק. שמואל has both words: 'ואתפלל בעדכם' (שמואל א ז:ה) and 'ויזעק שמואל' (שמואל א ז:ט). אליהו seems to have only prayer, so the switched version looks unsupported.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense (this part is fine)

phrases.english: Granted, regarding Samuel —
'prayer' is written about him
and 'crying' is written about him.
But regarding Elijah —
'prayer' is written, 'crying' is not written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's switched version
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברכה's ending should match the פסוק. No פסוק describes אליהו as crying out.

steps.title: Answer: 'Answer me, ה׳, answer me' is a form of crying
steps.stepSummary: אליהו's repeated plea 'עננו ה׳ עננו' counts as crying out.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Answer me, ה׳, answer me' is a way of crying out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that crying out is found with אליהו after all. His urgent, repeated words 'עננו ה׳ עננו' are a cry, even though the word 'צעקה' does not appear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts as 'crying' is the style of the plea, not the exact word. Repeating 'answer me' twice shows desperate pleading. So the switched version also fits the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: An expression, a form of speech

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of the endings are acceptable. שמואל has both 'prayer' and 'crying' in the פסוקים, and אליהו's 'עננו ה׳ עננו' counts as crying.

phrases.english: 'Answer me, Lord, answer me'
is an expression of crying.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲנֵנִי ה׳ עֲנֵנִי לְשׁוֹן צְעָקָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the פסוק: a word with the same meaning counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the actual word 'צעקה', אליהו did not cry out.
steps.terutzMaskana: A repeated, urgent plea is itself a צעקה.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes the משנה on the sixth and seventh ברכות
steps.stepSummary: The sixth ברכה mentions יונה and the seventh mentions דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the sixth ברכה he says: 'He Who answered יונה' and so on. For the seventh he says: 'He Who answered דוד' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another part of the משנה. This sets up a question about the order of the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה puts יונה sixth and דוד (with שלמה) seventh. Putting the two quotes side by side shows the order that the גמרא will ask about next.

phrases.english: For the sixth he says:
He Who answered Jonah, etc.
For the seventh he says:
He Who answered David, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה for a new point
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יונה is mentioned in the sixth ברכה and דוד in the seventh.

steps.title: Why is יונה mentioned before דוד?
steps.stepSummary: יונה lived after דוד and שלמה, so why does the משנה mention him first?
steps.simpleTranslation: After all, יונה lived after דוד and שלמה. So why does the משנה put him first?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the order. The list seems to follow history, but here a later figure comes before earlier ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list runs in time order: אברהם, the Sea, יהושע, שמואל, אליהו. יונה, a later נביא, breaks that pattern by coming before דוד and שלמה. The גמרא wants to know the reason.

phrases.english: After all, Jonah
lived after David and Solomon,
what is the reason he mentions him first?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי יוֹנָה בָּתַר דָּוִד וּשְׁלֹמֹה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the order in the quoted משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה breaks time order and puts יונה before דוד

steps.title: Answer: the series must end with 'מרחם על הארץ'
steps.stepSummary: דוד comes last because the final ברכה ends with 'מרחם על הארץ', which fits him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the משנה wants to end the series with 'מרחם על הארץ' (Who has mercy on the Land).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ending of the last ברכה decides the order. 'מרחם על הארץ' fits דוד and שלמה, so they go last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד and שלמה were kings of ארץ ישראל and prayed for the land. So their ברכה is the right one to end with 'mercy on the Land'. Ending the series well matters more here than keeping strict time order.

keyTerms.meaning: Who has mercy on the Land

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the order of ברכות can follow the theme of the ending rather than history.

phrases.english: Because he wants to conclude with
'Who has mercy on the Land.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דוד and שלמה go last so the series can end with 'מרחם על הארץ', which fits the kings of ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: סומכוס: the last ברכה ends 'Who humbles the exalted'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes סומכוס, who ends the final ברכה with 'משפיל הרמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: in the name of סומכוס they said the ending is 'Blessed are You... Who humbles the exalted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another opinion about how the last ברכה ends. According to סומכוס, it ends with 'משפיל הרמים' instead of 'מרחם על הארץ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second version of the closing words, not part of the answer about יונה. It gives a different theme for the final ברכה: הקב״ה humbling the proud.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, student of רבי מאיר

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the last ברכה's ending: the משנה's 'מרחם על הארץ' and סומכוס's 'משפיל הרמים'.

phrases.english: It was taught: in the name of Sumakhos they said:
'Blessed... Who humbles the exalted.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different ending for the last ברכה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to סומכוס, the final ברכה ends with 'ברוך משפיל הרמים'.

steps.title: Quoting the next line of the משנה about the priestly watch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on the first three fasts, the אנשי משמר fast but do not finish the fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first three fasts, the men of the priestly watch fast, but they do not complete the fast, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up a ברייתא that explains the rules about the אנשי משמר and the אנשי בית אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים were split into 24 groups called משמרות, and each group served in the בית המקדש for one week at a time. Each משמר was split again into smaller families called בתי אב, and each בית אב served on one day of that week. The משנה says the משמר does not finish the fast so they keep their strength for the עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the 24 priestly groups. Each served in the בית המקדש for one week.
A family within a משמר. Each served on one day of the week.
They complete (finish the fast until nightfall).
'Etc.', meaning the quote of the משנה continues.

phrases.english: On the first three fasts
the men of the priestly watch fast
but do not complete the fast, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה deals with wine for the משמר and the בית אב.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלֹשׁ תַּעֲנִיּוֹת הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר מִתְעַנִּין וְלֹא מַשְׁלִימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the ברכות of the fast day (סומכוס's ending) to a new line of the משנה about the כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first three fasts, the אנשי משמר fast but do not complete the fast.

steps.title: Why may the priestly watch drink wine only at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks why the אנשי משמר may drink wine at night but not during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: For what reason did they say that the men of the priestly watch may drink wine at night but not during the day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that asks for the reason behind the rule about the משמר and wine. This step only asks the question; the answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The puzzle is that the whole משמר is not on duty every day, since only one בית אב serves each day. So why should the rest of the משמר be stopped from drinking wine during the day? And why is night different?

keyTerms.meaning: 'The רבנן taught.' This introduces a ברייתא.
'For what reason did they say?' A request for the reason behind a rule.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
For what reason did they say
that the men of the watch are permitted to drink wine
at night but not during the day?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה's wine rule for the משמר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the אנשי משמר may drink wine at night but not by day.

steps.title: They may be called in to help during the day
steps.stepSummary: During the day, the work might become too heavy for the בית אב that is serving, and the rest of the משמר would be called in to help.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because maybe the Temple service will become too heavy for the men of the family that is serving, and the others will come and help them.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. The rest of the משמר might be called to help during the day, so they must stay sober.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day's עבודה belongs to one בית אב, but if there is too much work, the other כהנים of that week's משמר are close by and can be called in. A כהן who drank wine may not do the עבודה, so all of them must stay ready during the day. At night there is no such need, so wine is allowed then.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest; maybe (a worry about what could happen).

phrases.english: Lest the service become heavy
for the men of the family on duty,
and they (the משמר) will come and help them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא תִּכְבַּד הָעֲבוֹדָה עַל אַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משמר may be called to help the בית אב during the day, so they must be fit for עבודה.

steps.title: Why the family on duty may not drink wine at all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the אנשי בית אב may not drink wine, neither by day nor by night.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what reason did they say that the men of the family on duty may not drink wine, neither by day nor by night?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a second question, this time about the בית אב that is serving that day. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בית אב is stricter than the משמר, since it is forbidden even at night. The question is why night is also forbidden for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Neither by day nor by night.

phrases.english: For what reason did they say
that the men of the family on duty
may not drink, neither by day nor by night?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ אַנְשֵׁי בֵּית אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 11, now asking about the stricter rule for the בית אב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the בית אב is forbidden to drink wine even at night.

steps.title: They are busy with the service all the time
steps.stepSummary: The בית אב is constantly busy with the עבודה, day and night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they are always busy with the Temple service.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the בית אב on duty works around the clock, so wine is never allowed for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The serving family has jobs at night too, like burning the parts of the קרבנות on the מזבח. Since they are on duty all the time, there is no safe time for them to drink.

phrases.english: Because they are busy
constantly with the service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בית אב is always serving, day and night, so wine is never allowed for them.

steps.title: A כהן who knows his watch and his family's day
steps.stepSummary: A כהן today who knows both his משמר and his בית אב may not drink wine for that one whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: any כהן who knows his watch and the watch of his family, and knows that his ancestors were set there, may not drink wine that entire day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical rule from these reasons for a כהן today, after the חורבן. This is the first of three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the בית המקדש might be rebuilt suddenly, and his family would be called to serve on their day. If he knows exactly which day is his family's, he only has to avoid wine on that one day.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From here they said.' A practical rule drawn from what came before.
His ancestors' family was set there (as a fit, established part of the service).

steps.confusionAlert: This rule is about today, when there is no בית המקדש. The reason is that the בית המקדש could be rebuilt at any moment, and he must be ready to serve.

phrases.english: From here they said:
Any priest who knows his watch
and the watch (day) of his family,
and knows that his ancestors' family was set there
is forbidden to drink wine
that entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁמַּכִּיר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reasons of steps 12 and 14 to a כהן after the חורבן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If he knows both his week and his day, wine is forbidden only on that day.

steps.title: A כהן who knows only his watch
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who knows his משמר but not his בית אב may not drink wine that whole week.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he knows his watch but does not know the watch of his family, and knows that his ancestors were set there, he may not drink wine that entire week.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second case. He knows his family's week but not its day, so he must avoid wine for the whole week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since any day of that week might be his family's day, every day is a possible day of duty. Knowing less makes the time without wine longer.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means a week, not the day of שבת.

steps.confusionAlert: 'כׇּל אוֹתָהּ שַׁבָּת' means 'that whole week', the week his משמר served. It does not mean the day of שבת.

phrases.english: If he knows his watch

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַכִּיר מִשְׁמֶרֶת בֵּית אָב שֶׁלּוֹ,
phrases.english: but does not know the watch of his family,
and knows that his ancestors' family was set there
he is forbidden to drink wine
that entire week.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַכִּיר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ וְאֵין מַכִּיר מִשְׁמֶרֶת בֵּית אָב שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next case in the list: less knowledge, so a longer time without wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he knows his week but not his day, wine is forbidden the whole week.

steps.title: A כהן who knows neither his watch nor his family's day
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who knows neither his משמר nor his בית אב may not drink wine the whole year.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he knows neither his watch nor the watch of his family, but knows that his ancestors were set there, he may not drink wine the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case. He has no idea when his family served, so every day of the year could be his day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no information at all, there is no day that is safe. So by the strict letter of this ברייתא, wine is forbidden all year.
steps.whatToRemember: There is a ladder here. The משמר may not drink by day, because they might be called to help. The בית אב may not drink day or night, because they are always serving. A כהן today must avoid wine for one day, one week, or the whole year, depending on how much he knows about when his family served.

phrases.english: If he does not know his watch
or the watch of his family,
but knows that his ancestors' family was set there
he is forbidden to drink wine
the whole year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ מַכִּיר מִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ וּמִשְׁמֶרֶת בֵּית אָב שֶׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list with the case of least knowledge and the longest time without wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he knows neither his week nor his day, wine is forbidden all year.

steps.title: רבי: strictly, no כהן should ever drink wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the logic of the earlier rules should forbid every כהן from ever drinking wine, but such a rule would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: I say it should be forbidden to drink wine forever. But what can I do? His misfortune is his remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי takes the earlier rules about wine one step further. Then he explains why that stricter rule cannot actually be made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a כהן who knows his משמר cannot be sure the order of the משמרות will stay the same when the בית המקדש is rebuilt. So logically, every כהן should always stay ready and never drink. But the בית המקדש has been destroyed for so long that a permanent ban is not practical. The very length of the חורבן is what makes it possible to be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: What can I do? (a sigh: the ideal rule cannot be kept)
Literally 'his fixing is his ruin.' Here it works the other way: his misfortune (the long חורבן) is what fixes the problem.

steps.confusionAlert: Read the phrase תקנתו קלקלתו in context. Here it means that the misfortune of the long חורבן is what lets כהנים drink. It does not mean that רבי's rule causes damage.

phrases.english: Rebbi says: I say:
it is forbidden to drink wine forever,
but what can I do,
for his misfortune is his remedy.
phrases.notes: The long destruction makes a permanent ban unrealistic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the logic of Steps 15-17 to its extreme and then limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally no כהן should ever drink wine, but this cannot be enforced because the חורבן has lasted so long.

steps.title: אביי: כהנים today drink wine following רבי
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the common practice of כהנים drinking wine today follows רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Following whom do כהנים drink wine nowadays? Following רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי ties the real-world practice of his day to רבי's opinion. This closes the topic of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the earlier rules, a כהן who does not know his משמר should not drink all year, and today almost no כהן knows his משמר. The only reason כהנים drink at all is רבי's point that the long חורבן makes such a ban impossible to keep.
steps.whatToRemember: כהנים today may drink wine. This follows רבי: since the חורבן has lasted so long, the strict logic of 'stay ready for the עבודה' is not enforced.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
following whom do priests drink wine nowadays?
Following Rebbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי's view (Step 18) to current practice.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Today's practice of כהנים drinking wine rests on רבי's opinion.

steps.title: The משנה: no haircuts or laundry for the watch, except on Thursday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: אנשי משמר and אנשי מעמד may not cut hair or launder during their week, but they may on Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: The men of the משמר and the men of the מעמד are forbidden to cut their hair and to launder. On Thursday they are permitted, out of respect for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It quotes this line to set up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts here. The ban covers the whole week of service. Thursday is an exception so that people are groomed for שבת. The reason for the ban itself is not stated yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Representatives of the Jewish people who stood by the קרבנות during that week

phrases.english: The men of the watch and the men of the standing group
are forbidden to cut hair and to launder,
but on Thursday they are permitted
because of the honor of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר וְאַנְשֵׁי מַעֲמָד אֲסוּרִים לְסַפֵּר וּלְכַבֵּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the wine topic and quotes a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Haircuts and laundry are forbidden during the week of the watch, but permitted on Thursday for כבוד שבת.

steps.title: Why the ban on haircuts and laundry?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה's ban.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why haircuts and laundry were forbidden during the watch. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance the ban seems strange, since grooming looks like a good thing for people serving in the בית המקדש. So the גמרא needs to explain it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for banning haircuts and laundry during the watch.

steps.title: So they groom before their watch begins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the ban pushes them to groom before the week starts, so they do not arrive messy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: So that they will not enter their watch while unkempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the ban. It is meant to make the men groom before their week of service begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If grooming were allowed during the week, people might put it off and show up messy, planning to fix it later. Forbidding it during the week forces them to get ready ahead of time. So the ban actually protects their neat appearance.
steps.confusionAlert: The ban does not mean grooming is bad. Its purpose is the opposite: to make sure they are well groomed when the week begins.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
so that they will not enter their watch
while they are unkempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban forces them to groom before the watch, so they do not serve while unkempt.

steps.title: ברייתא: haircut schedules for מלך, כהן גדול, and כהן הדיוט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sets how often each person cuts his hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A מלך cuts his hair every day. A כהן גדול cuts it every ערב שבת. A כהן הדיוט cuts it once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא about haircut schedules. The steps that follow explain each part of it one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three levels of how often to cut hair, from most often to least often. It gives no reasons. The גמרא will supply the reasons next.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
a king cuts his hair every day,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל — מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: a High Priest, from Friday to Friday,
a common priest, once every thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֶלֶךְ מִסְתַּפֵּר בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the grooming theme from Step 22 with a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלך cuts his hair daily, a כהן גדול weekly, and a כהן הדיוט every thirty days.

steps.title: Why does the king cut his hair daily?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the king's daily haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: A מלך cuts his hair every day. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through the ברייתא, beginning with the מלך. The answer follows in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A haircut every day is unusually often. That calls for a source.

phrases.english: A king cuts his hair every day:
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶלֶךְ מִסְתַּפֵּר בְּכׇל יוֹם — מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first clause of the ברייתא in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for a king's daily haircut.

steps.title: The king must be seen in his beauty
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא בר זבדא cites ישעיהו: 'Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא בר זבדא said: The verse says, 'Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that teaches that a king must always look his best.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since people see the king all the time, he must always look beautiful. That requires grooming every day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said:
the verse says:
"Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: מֶלֶךְ בְּיׇפְיוֹ תֶּחֱזֶינָה עֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A פסוק requires the king always to appear in his beauty.

steps.title: Why does the כהן גדול cut his hair every Friday?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the כהן גדול's weekly haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן גדול cuts his hair from ערב שבת to ערב שבת. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second part of the ברייתא. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a week is less often than the king's daily haircut but more often than every thirty days. The גמרא wants to know why this middle level applies.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: A High Priest, from Friday to Friday:
what is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת — מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the second clause of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the כהן גדול's weekly haircut.

steps.title: Because a new watch arrives every week
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יצחק explains that the משמרות change every week, so the כהן גדול should look fresh for each new group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יצחק said: Because the משמרות are renewed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the weekly haircut. A new משמר comes in each week, and the כהן גדול should look his best for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משמרות change at שבת. So on Friday the כהן גדול grooms himself, and each incoming group sees him looking fresh and dignified.

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yitzḥak said:
since the watches are renewed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The weekly change of משמרות calls for the כהן גדול to groom each week.

steps.title: Where do we learn the כהן הדיוט's thirty days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the כהן הדיוט's thirty-day haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן הדיוט cuts his hair once every thirty days. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the last part of the ברייתא and asks for a source, not just a reason. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גמרא asks מנלן ('from where do we know this?') instead of מאי טעמא ('what is the reason?'). The exact number thirty needs a textual source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: A common priest once every thirty days:
from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט אַחַת לִשְׁלשִׁים יוֹם — מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the third clause of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the thirty-day interval.

steps.title: Learning פרע from נזיר: thirty days
steps.stepSummary: A גזירה שוה on the word פרע links כהנים to נזיר. Just as a נזיר's growth is thirty days, so is a כהן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from the word 'פרע' here and 'פרע' in נזיר. Here it is written: 'They shall not shave their heads, nor let their locks (פרע) grow long.' There it is written: 'He shall be holy, he shall let the locks (פרע) of the hair of his head grow.' Just as there it is thirty days, so here it is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word, פרע, appears both for כהנים and for נזיר, so the time period is carried over from one to the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For כהנים the פסוק says not to let פרע (grown hair) grow out, but it does not say how long counts as 'grown.' For נזיר, the standard period of נזירות, when no time is specified, is thirty days, so פרע means thirty days of growth. That definition is applied to כהנים: they may not go past thirty days without a haircut.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived (via a גזירה שוה)
Just as there... so too here (the formula of a גזירה שוה)

steps.confusionAlert: The thirty days come from the standard length of נזירות when no time is specified (סתם נזירות). They do not come from anything stated about כהנים themselves.
steps.whatToRemember: A מלך grooms daily (to be seen in his beauty), a כהן גדול weekly (for each new משמר), and a כהן הדיוט every thirty days (גזירה שוה of פרע from נזיר).

phrases.english: It is derived from 'pera' and 'pera' from the nazirite.
It is written here:
"Neither shall they shave their heads
nor let their locks grow long,"
and it is written there:
"He shall be holy;
he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow,"
just as there it is thirty,
so too here it is thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 28 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on פרע from נזיר sets thirty days as the limit for a כהן.

steps.title: Where does the נזיר's own thirty days come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a נזיר's hair growth period is thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the נזיר himself, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא just learned the כהן's thirty days from the נזיר through a גזירה שוה. Now it asks how we know that the נזיר himself has thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה only works if the original case is clear. Since the כהן's rule depends on the נזיר's, the גמרא needs a firm source for the נזיר's thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow to avoid wine and haircuts and to stay away from contact with the dead
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: And the nazirite himself, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the base case that step 29 relied on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a נזיר's period is thirty days

steps.title: An unspecified נזירות lasts thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה states the rule that a plain, unspecified נזירות is thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: An unspecified נזירות is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מתנה answers with a known rule. If someone becomes a נזיר without saying how long, the נזירות lasts thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the basic length of נזירות, which the כהנים' haircut rule is built on. The rule itself still needs a source, so the next step asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A נזירות vow taken without saying how long it lasts

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said:
An unspecified naziriteship is thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A plain נזירות is thirty days

steps.title: Where does the thirty-day rule come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of רב מתנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how we know that a plain נזירות is thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מתנה stated a rule but did not give a source. The גמרא wants to see where it comes from in the תורה.

phrases.english: From where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 31
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that gives the thirty-day length

steps.title: The word 'יהיה' adds up to thirty
steps.stepSummary: The word 'יהיה' in the נזיר section has a גימטריא of thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'יהיה' (he shall be holy), and its numerical value is thirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from the word 'יהיה' in the פסוק about the נזיר. Its letters add up to thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters are י (10) + ה (5) + י (10) + ה (5) = 30. So 'he shall be holy' is read as 'he shall be holy for thirty days.'

keyTerms.meaning: The numerical value of a word's letters
'He shall be' (the word adds up to 30)

phrases.english: The verse states: 'He shall be'
In numerical value it is thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 32 with a פסוק
steps.whatToRemember: The thirty days of a כהן's hair come from the נזיר through the גזירה שוה of 'פרע'. The נזיר's own thirty days come from the גימטריא of 'יהיה'.

steps.title: Maybe כהנים may not grow their hair at all
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that the פסוק means כהנים may not let their hair grow at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But maybe this is what the תורה is saying: they should not grow hair at all!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the reading of the פסוק about כהנים. Maybe it means they must not grow any hair at all, and not that thirty days of growth is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ופרע לא ישלחו.' רב פפא reads it as a total ban on long hair, which would mean cutting it constantly. That would cancel the thirty-day limit.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
They should not grow it at all

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying:
They should not grow it at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the כהנים פסוק behind the thirty-day rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that כהנים may grow hair up to thirty days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could be read as a total ban on growing hair

steps.title: The word order shows that some hair is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves from the word order that hair is allowed, and only long growth is banned.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If it were written 'they shall not grow long hair,' it would be as you say. Now that it is written 'and hair, they shall not grow long,' it means: hair they may have, they just may not let it grow long.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא by pointing to the order of the words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'פרע' (hair) first, then 'לא ישלחו' (do not let it grow long). This means some hair is allowed and only excessive growth is forbidden. So the thirty-day limit stands.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it were written
'They shall not grow long locks', it would be as you said;
now that it is written: 'And locks they shall not grow long'
let there be locks,
it is only growing them long that they may not do.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No hair growth is allowed at all
steps.terutzMaskana: Hair is allowed; only long growth (beyond thirty days) is forbidden

steps.title: Then כהנים should cut their hair even today
steps.stepSummary: If the haircut is a Torah requirement, כהנים today should also cut their hair every thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even nowadays too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: if this is Torah law, כהנים should keep it even today, in case the מקדש is rebuilt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Torah rule usually does not simply lapse. Since the בית המקדש could be rebuilt at any moment, כהנים would need to be ready.

phrases.english: If so, even nowadays as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the confirmed Torah rule and asks why it is not kept today
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice that כהנים today do not keep the thirty-day haircut
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah rule tied to readiness for service should apply always

steps.title: Like wine, it only applies when entering the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The haircut rule is compared to the ban on wine, which applies only at the time of entering the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like those who drank wine. Just as with wine, it is forbidden only at the time of entering the מקדש, and outside that time it is allowed, so too here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by comparing the haircut rule to the rule for a כהן who drank wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on שתויי יין only applies when a כהן actually enters for service. In the same way, long hair is a problem only at the time of service. Today there is no service, so there is no requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of entering the מקדש

phrases.english: It is similar to those who have drunk wine.
Just as those who have drunk wine,
it is at the time of entering that it is forbidden,
not at the time of entering, it is permitted,
so too here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The haircut rule applies at all times
steps.terutzMaskana: Like wine, it applies only at the time of service

steps.title: רבי says כהנים should never drink wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי saying that כהנים should really be forbidden to drink wine at all times.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי says, I say that כהנים are forbidden to drink wine at all times, but what can I do, since his damage is his repair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wine comparison with a ברייתא. רבי holds that wine should really be forbidden to כהנים at all times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's reasoning is that the מקדש could be rebuilt at any moment, so in principle every כהן should always be ready. He permits wine only because of תקנתו קלקלתו: the חורבן has lasted so long that a permanent ban cannot be kept. The challenge comes from the implication: if כהנים drink today only because of רבי, then the רבנן forbid wine today. That means the wine ban is not limited to the time of entering, so the comparison in step 37 breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא
His damage is his repair: the very problem is what allows it

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi says:
I say that priests are forbidden
to drink wine at all times,
but what can I do,
for his misfortune is his remedy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wine comparison of step 37
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the wine ban applies only at the time of entering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי himself allows wine. But the ברייתא together with אביי's remark implies that the רבנן, who disagree with רבי, forbid כהנים wine even nowadays, because the מקדש might be rebuilt soon. If wine is forbidden today, it is not limited to the time of entering, and the comparison of step 37 would require haircuts today as well.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not actually forbid wine. He says it should be forbidden, but it is allowed only because of תקנתו קלקלתו.

steps.title: אביי asks whose view lets כהנים drink wine today
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks according to whom כהנים drink wine nowadays; the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: According to whom do כהנים drink wine nowadays?
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. אביי asks whose view allows כהנים to drink wine today, and his answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's question suggests that only one opinion (רבי's) allows wine today. If so, the other view would forbid it, and that would weaken the comparison in step 37.

phrases.english: And Abaye said:
In accordance with whom do priests drink wine nowadays?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds אביי's comment to strengthen the challenge from רבי's ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion is the basis for כהנים drinking wine today (answered on the next amud)
